text:
Recent work supports testing candidate discrimination before changing context architecture, but does not establish it as this task’s bottleneck. [Context-Aware Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11021640) conditions sampling on temporal context; its reported benefit is primarily diversity (+20.65%), with a small accuracy loss (1.89%), so it provides limited evidence for improving HR@10. More directly relevant, [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) uses uniform-negative warm-up, global candidate recall, and curriculum-controlled hardness. Experiments across five sequential backbones support treating sampling difficulty as an optimization variable.

Hardest-negative selection risks penalizing plausible positives. [Hard-BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies the pairwise objective to reduce false-negative influence under dynamic hard sampling; [AHNS (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) adapts hardness rather than fixing it. Both offer transferable ideas, though their collaborative-filtering results do not establish gains for NextItNet. A practical hypothesis is uniform warm-up followed by a mixture of uniform and moderately hard candidates scored by the same NextItNet, excluding known training positives and limiting extreme-negative influence. This requires no additional predictor or unavailable attributes.

Keep uniform multi-negative cross-entropy as the control: a [2024 sequential sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) found dataset-dependent accuracy/popularity trade-offs, while [2025 loss analysis](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11228603) shows full-catalog loss advantages need not carry over under sampling. Compare sampling and robust-loss changes separately at matched compute using unchanged macro validation HR@10. Industrial’s weak training separation motivates this experiment; CD training margins alone cannot demonstrate generalization.
